template_fix.added_instruction: For each action-plan item, give the owner and the time window only if the source states them. If the source does not name an owner, or gives no date or time window, write exactly `Not stated in source` in that field. Never supply an owner, team, date or deadline the source does not give.

claims.claim: Section templates + length bounds control output cost
claims.measured: same model (Sonnet): −54%; + Haiku: −98%; 1-section regen vs full re-draft: −49%
claims.note: The cost claim holds, but the saving is not free: graded blind, the templated drafts score lower on accuracy (3.92 → 3.08 / 2.58) and have more serious errors (1 → 6 / 10); see the quality table and the implicit-claim row.

claims.measured: head-to-head: templated drafts preferred over the unbounded draft in 0/16 comparisons (0 ties; 95% Wilson 0–19%); accuracy 3.92 unbounded vs 3.08 / 2.58 (Sonnet / Haiku template), coverage 4.92 vs 4.00 / 3.50; serious errors 1 vs 6 / 10. Not worse: core facts 32/32 vs 32/32 / 32/32. Better: clarity 4.00 vs 4.92 / 4.42, concision 2.83 vs 4.17 / 4.08
claims.note: Blind LLM judge (`claude-opus-5-5`, not one of the models under test; 3 rubric passes per draft; every pair shown in both orders, position-consistent in 11/12 pairs), one draft per rung × 4 documents; the lead verified the serious errors against the source payloads. Shorter drafts keep every core fact and read better, but they are less accurate and less complete and lose every head-to-head comparison. The template requires an owner and a time window for every action item; the grader flagged an owner or deadline the source does not support in 16 of 24 templated action items (12 with a serious error). A single judge may favour longer drafts (its prompt tells it to ignore length and layout), but the serious errors were verified against the sources, so they do not rest on the judge's taste. Follow-up (not the app's template): one added sentence letting the template write "Not stated in source" cut serious errors per draft from 1.25 / 2.25 to 0.00 / 0.25 (Sonnet / Haiku, 12 fresh drafts each) and raised accuracy from 3.25 / 2.67 to 4.17 / 3.83, but actionability fell (3.67 / 3.25 → 3.08 / 2.67) and the long draft is still preferred in 15 of 16 comparisons. This row grades the template as the app ships it.

claims.claim: Prefix caching + sliding-window summary prevents quadratic session cost
claims.measured: context slope: naive +1247 tok/turn → summarized +288 tok/turn (peak 15.6k); cost −47% billed (n=6 sessions per rung); quality trade-off: recall questions 2/36 vs 36/36 with cached full history, turn 1–3 details kept in the final summary 24/51 vs 39/51
claims.note: Caching alone cuts cost −40% but context still grows +1197 tok/turn (quadratic session total). Only summarization bounds the growth. The cost claim holds, but the saving is not free: compaction drops early-turn specifics, which the assistant then declines to recall (see the quality table and the implicit-claim row).

claims.measured: answers grounded (turns 1–9): 205/207 summarized vs 203/207 cached full history; recall questions 2/36 vs 36/36; turn 1–3 details in final summary 24/51 vs 39/51
claims.note: Answer key, deterministic string matching, 95% Wilson intervals. Replies on turns 1–9 stay grounded on every rung, but once early turns are compacted the assistant can no longer recall their specifics and the final summary keeps fewer of them. Caching alone changes no quality measure.

claims.claim: Pair hybrid retrieval (reranking + chunk filtering) with context caching
claims.measured: paired rung (Haiku picks 5 clauses from the cached full corpus, Sonnet answers over them; n=24 per corpus size): expected clauses kept 100% / 100% (7 / 21 documents) vs BM25+rerank 99% / 86%; other suppliers' clauses selected 0/120 vs 25/120; $/question billed $0.0244 / $0.0264 vs BM25+rerank $0.0247 / $0.0278 and cached full corpus $0.0253 / $0.0379; grader correctness 4.54 / 4.38 vs cached full corpus 4.96 / 4.83; answers with a serious error 1/24 / 6/24 vs 0/24 / 0/24
claims.note: Pairing works on retrieval and cost: reranking over the cached corpus finds every expected clause at both corpus sizes, picks no other supplier's clause, and is the cheapest version per question billed in 8-question sessions. It does not match the cached full corpus on answer quality: with 5 clauses the answering model sometimes states that the documents contain no gate or term that is in a clause it was not sent. Warm, the cached full corpus is cheaper per question; it overtakes the paired rung once 10 (7 documents) / 23 (21 documents) questions share one cache write. Verdict: cost and retrieval hold; quality does not hold against the version without retrieval.

claims.measured: answers with a serious error (7 / 21 documents, n=24 each): naive 1/24 / 3/24, cached full corpus 0/24 / 0/24, BM25+rerank 0/24 / 8/24, paired 1/24 / 6/24; grader correctness naive 4.50 / 4.50, cached 4.96 / 4.83, BM25+rerank 4.71 / 3.96, paired 4.54 / 4.38; key facts BM25+rerank 152/159 / 145/159 vs cached 150/159 / 149/159
claims.note: Rule: a lever loses quality when its share of answers with a serious error is clearly higher (95% Wilson intervals do not overlap) than the full-corpus version it replaces (the cached full corpus) at the same corpus size. Caching the full corpus loses nothing (it has the fewest serious errors at both sizes). Retrieval loses nothing on the 7-document deal room; at 21 documents BM25+rerank does (8/24 vs 0/24), and the paired rung's 6/24 is higher but its interval still overlaps. Against the naive full corpus the retrieval rungs' intervals overlap. Blind grader, one pass per answer; the deterministic key facts move less than the grader's error count.

claims.claim: Isolate sub-agent contexts, cache the shared repo prefix, measure cost per verified outcome (CpO)
claims.measured: CpO per verified fix: Shared bus, original instructions $0.696 (15/15 verified); Shared bus, matched instructions + gate $0.469 (15/15 verified); Isolated + cached repo prefix + gate $0.100 (15/15 verified); Tiered: Haiku agents + Sonnet patch author $0.056 (15/15 verified)
claims.note: Cost per verified fix falls ~12× from the shared bus to the tiered swarm (isolation + caching alone, same instructions: $0.469 → $0.100), while the verified rate is the same in every arm. The tasks are too easy to show a quality effect (ceiling): every saving is cost per run, and CpO adds nothing over it here, so the outcome side of the claim is untested.

claims.claim: Monotonic token scale: Cat 1 < Cat 2 < Cat 3 < Cat 4 < Cat 5 << Cat 6
claims.measured: Cat 1 (item) 1.5k; Cat 2 (document) 8.5k; Cat 3 (10-turn session) 169.6k; Cat 4 (4-question audit) 77.5k; Cat 4 (single question) 19.4k; Cat 4 (single question, 3× corpus) 55.1k; Cat 5 (invoice) 116.9k; Cat 6 (incident run, shared bus) 267.3k
claims.note: 1 < 2 < {3,4,5} < 6 holds. The order of 3, 4 and 5 depends on the unit: a 10-turn session bills more than a single RAG question or a whole invoice.
